answer.reason: Clicks exist on Meta, Google Ads, LinkedIn and organic search, and they are not the same thing.
Three ad platforms and two account currencies: one number would add dollars to euros.
CPC is defined per platform, and blended CPC only within one currency.
Meta ad CTR and organic search CTR are both called CTR.
Ad impressions on three platforms and search impressions share the word and nothing else.
GA4 key events, Google Ads conversions and LinkedIn conversions count different things.
The three count overlapping events with different attribution; GA4 key events already include visits the ad platforms claim. Their sum is not a number of conversions.
The accounts bill in US dollars and euros; a single total adds two currencies.
Invoices are paid in US dollars and euros; a single total adds two currencies.
Revenue and spend each mix two currencies; the ratio of the mixed sums means nothing.
No period and no currency: any number picks both silently.
The campaign runs on three platforms and the question names no measure.
Reach is per campaign and day; a person reached on two days counts twice in any sum.
GA4 users are distinct per day; the warehouse holds daily rows, so a month cannot be deduplicated.
Frequency over a month needs the month's deduplicated reach, which daily rows cannot give.
Age exists on Meta spend only; Stripe revenue cannot be split by the buyer's age bracket.
Channel type exists on Google spend only; new customers cannot be assigned to one.
Ad spend is not known per customer; dividing each customer's revenue by all spend is not ROAS.
Leads carry a form id, spend does not; spend cannot be allocated to a form.
Net revenue comes from balance transactions, which carry no attribution.
No device breakdown of Meta is loaded; placements are not devices.
Two grains of the same clicks: adding them counts every attributed click twice.
TikTok is not a source in the warehouse.
No email platform is loaded; GA4 only sees the sessions the newsletter sent.
Lead answers are personal data and never leave raw; the agent cannot read them.
The agent sees paid invoices only; open and void ones stay in raw.
The read path cannot change a platform or the warehouse (DESIGN.md §1).
The warehouse holds what happened; it has no forecast and no budget plan for future months.

answer.reason: Clicks exist on Meta, Google Ads, LinkedIn and organic search, and they are not the same thing.
Three ad platforms and two account currencies: one number would add dollars to euros.
CPC is defined per platform, and blended CPC only within one currency.
Meta ad CTR and organic search CTR are both called CTR.
Ad impressions on three platforms and search impressions share the word and nothing else.
GA4 key events, Google Ads conversions and LinkedIn conversions count different things.
The three count overlapping events with different attribution; GA4 key events already include visits the ad platforms claim. Their sum is not a number of conversions.
The accounts bill in US dollars and euros; a single total adds two currencies.
Invoices are paid in US dollars and euros; a single total adds two currencies.
Revenue and spend each mix two currencies; the ratio of the mixed sums means nothing.
No period and no currency: any number picks both silently.
The campaign runs on three platforms and the question names no measure.
Reach is per campaign and day; a person reached on two days counts twice in any sum.
GA4 users are distinct per day; the warehouse holds daily rows, so a month cannot be deduplicated.
Frequency over a month needs the month's deduplicated reach, which daily rows cannot give.
Age exists on Meta spend only; Stripe revenue cannot be split by the buyer's age bracket.
Channel type exists on Google spend only; new customers cannot be assigned to one.
Ad spend is not known per customer; dividing each customer's revenue by all spend is not ROAS.
Leads carry a form id, spend does not; spend cannot be allocated to a form.
Net revenue comes from balance transactions, which carry no attribution.
No device breakdown of Meta is loaded; placements are not devices.
Two grains of the same clicks: adding them counts every attributed click twice.
TikTok is not a source in the warehouse.
No email platform is loaded; GA4 only sees the sessions the newsletter sent.
Lead answers are personal data and never leave raw; the agent cannot read them.
The agent sees paid invoices only; open and void ones stay in raw.
The read path cannot change a platform or the warehouse (DESIGN.md §1).
The warehouse holds what happened; it has no forecast and no budget plan for future months.
